statements.impact_statement: Measured 2026-11-09 on the apache-activemq-6.3.3-bin.tar.gz release the image is built from. CVE-2026-56130 is the Shiro remember-me cookie not being checked for expiry on the server; that cookie handling is shiro-web's CookieRememberMeManager. The release ships three Shiro jars, all under lib/optional: shiro-core-2.2.1, shiro-spring-2.2.1 and activemq-shiro-6.3.3 (tar -tzf); there is no shiro-web jar, so CookieRememberMeManager is not in the image. A byte scan of every class found 0 remember-me references in activemq-shiro (ActiveMQ's own ShiroPlugin, which builds a DefaultSecurityManager whose remember-me manager defaults to null) and only in shiro-spring's Spring configuration classes, which need the absent shiro-web classes and which ActiveMQ never imports; the shipped conf/activemq.xml does not mention Shiro at all. The fix exists only in Shiro 3.0.0, a major line ActiveMQ 6.3 does not use. Revisit if an ActiveMQ release adds shiro-web.

PROVEN false-positive. Measured 2026-11-01. CVE-2026-111943 is a Go standard library flaw (crypto/x509 accepts untrusted intermediate certificates); Wolfi's secdb files it against the grpc-1.83 origin, so every subpackage inherits it and the fix revision 1.83.1-r6 is not in the public index (newest py3.12-grpcio-1.83 is 1.83.1-r0). The subpackage this image ships contains no Go code: extracting py3.12-grpcio-1.83-1.83.1-r0.apk gives 140 files, all Python sources, dist-info, BUILD.bazel files and one native module, grpc/_cython/cygrpc.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so, a Cython/C++ extension whose .PKGINFO depends only on abseil, c-ares, re2, OpenSSL, zlib and libstdc++. readelf -S on that .so lists no .go.buildinfo, .gopclntab or .note.go.buildid section and strings finds no crypto/x509. or runtime.goexit symbol, so the Go crypto/x509 code the advisory names is not present.

GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc makes rand unsound only when BOTH its log and thread_rng features are enabled and a custom logger calls rand::rng() while ThreadRng reseeds; the unsafe path is the log call inside the reseeding core. rand 0.9.2 reaches the image only in Wolfi libpathrs 0.2.5 (/usr/lib/libpathrs.so.0.2.5, a runc dependency), built from tag v0.2.5 commit 080908395e75a32a5c4dbe9b318bf93643429f9f with that tag Cargo.lock, which ships at /usr/share/doc/libpathrs/Cargo.lock. libpathrs Cargo.toml:78 declares rand = { version = "0.9", optional = true } with default features (no log), and the lock entry for rand 0.9.2 lists only rand_chacha and rand_core as dependencies: log, the optional dependency the log feature enables, is not resolved, so the log feature and the logging calls in rand are not compiled into the library. The recipe fails the build if libpathrs leaves 0.2.5 or the rand lock entry gains log. Verified 2026-10-13.

PROVEN false-positive, measured 2026-10-08 on calico-node 3.32.0. The advisory is Wolfi's, keyed to the package calico-node-3.32 3.32.0-r4 (fixed in 3.32.2-r3, a revision not in the public APKINDEX on 2026-10-08), and its vulnerable code is the Go module github.com/gopacket/gopacket linked into that package's Go binaries. Listing every ELF file of calico-node-3.32-3.32.0-r4.apk and checking each for Go build info showed exactly two Go binaries, /usr/bin/calico-node and /usr/bin/mountns; the rest are the C BIRD daemons and BPF objects in /usr/lib/calico/bpf. This image replaces both binaries with quench-calico-node (melange `replaces: calico-node-3.32`), built from the v3.32.0 tag with the floor pass. Verified by the build itself: melange.yaml runs `go version -m` on both replacement binaries and fails if github.com/gopacket/gopacket is below v1.6.1; and the gate's binary scan of /usr/bin/calico-node (run 37707336807) reported none of these advisories, only cel-go, since floored. The vulnerable github.com/gopacket/gopacket code is therefore not present in the image; only the package record of the replaced apk still carries the version.

PROVEN false-positive, measured 2026-09-29 on 8.3.1. CVE-2020-5415 is Concourse's own advisory (GitLab login mapped the user's display name to the user identity, allowing impersonation). Its fixed versions mix two version spaces: Concourse releases 6.3.1 and 6.4.1, and a concourse/dex pseudo-version 0.0.0-20200730150203-821b48abfd88. The dex fork is now tagged v1.14.0 (committer date 2026-05-19), which sorts below 6.3.1, so every current dex release matches by construction. Checked the code rather than the numbers: in v1.14.0 connector/gitlab/gitlab.go sets PreferredUsername to user.Username (the GitLab login) and Username to the display name; Concourse 8.3.1 authorizes team membership on the token's preferred_username first (atc/api/accessor/accessor.go:236, userName() returns the preferred_username claim when set), and skymarshal passes claims.PreferredUsername to its display user id generator (skymarshal/token/access_token.go:108-114). The identity Concourse matches against a team's GitLab user allow-list is therefore the login, which a user cannot set to someone else's; the display name the 2020 flaw keyed on is not what authorizes.

CVE-2026-33997 is a privilege-validation bypass in the Moby daemon's plugin installation. connaisseur (./cmd/connaisseur) imports only github.com/docker/docker/registry and api/types/registry, in internal/validator/notaryv1/notaryserver/client.go:20-21 and simple_cred_store.go:7, to authenticate against Notary v1 registries. Checked with `go list -deps ./cmd/connaisseur` at v3.11.1, v3.12.0 and v3.13.0: no daemon, plugin manager or API server package is in the build. The build fails if one is ever linked. The fix (29.3.1) exists only under the github.com/moby/moby module path, so the +incompatible module cannot be floated to it.

GHSA-7gcf-g7xr-8hxj is a panic in serde_with's KeyValueMap serializer. nixpacks 1.41.0 (the last release; serde_with 2.x, fix only in 3.21.0) uses serde_with only for the #[serde_with::skip_serializing_none] attribute (src/nixpacks/nix/pkg.rs:5, plan/phase.rs:14 and :50, plan/mod.rs:29); grep for KeyValueMap over nixpacks src returned 0 matches. KeyValueMap is a generic serde_as adapter that is only compiled when named, so its code is not in the binary. The recipe fails the build if nixpacks ever names KeyValueMap. Verified 2026-10-13.

GHSA-mc8h-8q98-g5hr is a TOCTOU race in remove_dir_all's own directory walk. nixpacks reaches remove_dir_all 0.5.3 only through tempdir 0.3.7 (TempDir drop, tempdir src/lib.rs:326). Read the source of remove_dir_all 0.5.3: src/lib.rs compiles its own fs module only under cfg(windows) and on every other target is `pub use std::fs::remove_dir_all`, so this Linux image runs the standard library implementation (rust 1.96, which carries the CVE-2022-21658 fix), not the vulnerable walk. The 0.5 line has no fixed release. Verified 2026-10-13.

The advisory: minimatch before 11.0.1 expands attacker-controlled **/.. segments in firstPhasePreProcess() and compares them pairwise in secondPhasePreProcess(), run at optimizationLevel 2 or higher. Those functions and the optimizationLevel option arrived with the minimatch 7+ rewrite. Verified 2026-11-02 on the npm tarball minimatch-5.1.8.tgz (sha256 3effb35e05b4291721c5a37775dfcf9350cf7a031def3f7b674ecc638219cd4a): grep -c 'firstPhasePreProcess\|optimizationLevel' returned 0 for package/minimatch.js and package/lib/path.js, the only JavaScript files it ships. 5.1.8 is the glob-scoped copy under pm2's glob 8, which needs minimatch ^5.

CVE-2025-4432 (RUSTSEC-2025-0009) is a panic in ring's AES functions (AES-GCM / QUIC header protection counter arithmetic) when overflow checks are on. Cosmian KMS 5.27.0 links ring 0.16.20 only through scratchstack-aws-signature 0.10.6 (Cargo.lock at tag 5.27.0: it is the only package listing ring 0.16.20; 5.27.1 and 5.28.0 carry no ring 0.16). Read the source of scratchstack-aws-signature 0.10.6: it imports only ring::hmac (src/hmac.rs:1, HMAC_SHA256) and ring::digest (src/signature.rs:20, SHA256); no ring::aead or AES call exists, grep for aead|aes over its src returned 0 matches. The AES code is therefore never executed. ring 0.16 has no fixed release (fix is 0.17.12). The recipe fails the build if any other crate depends on ring 0.16. Verified 2026-10-13.

Measured 2026-11-09 on the published datahub-frontend 1.8.0 and 1.7.0.1 images (crane export). CVE-2026-56130 is the Shiro remember-me cookie not being checked for expiry on the server; that cookie handling is shiro-web's CookieRememberMeManager. Both images ship the same eleven Shiro 2.2.1 jars in datahub-frontend/lib (cache, config-core, config-ogdl, core, crypto-cipher, crypto-core, crypto-hash, event, hashes-argon2, hashes-bcrypt, lang) and no shiro-web jar, so CookieRememberMeManager is not in the image. A byte scan of every non-Shiro jar in 1.8.0 found only two classes that reference org/apache/shiro: DataHub's auth/pac4j/Shiro2AesDataEncrypter (AesCipherService, ByteSource: pac4j session encryption) and pac4j-core's ShiroPasswordEncoder (hashing). Neither touches a SecurityManager or remember-me; DataHub authenticates through pac4j and Play sessions, not Shiro subjects. The fix exists only in Shiro 3.0.0, a major line DataHub does not use.

CVE-2026-33997 is a privilege-validation bypass in the Moby daemon's plugin installation. dive (main package .) links only the API types and the client from the module: github.com/docker/docker/api, api/types/* and client, plus github.com/moby/moby/api/types/plugin (types only). Checked with `go list -deps .` at v0.13.1 with docker v28.5.2: no daemon, plugin manager or API server package is in the build, and dive never calls the client's plugin endpoints. The build fails if a daemon, plugin or api/server package is ever linked. The fix (29.3.1) exists only under the github.com/moby/moby module path, so the +incompatible module cannot be floated to it.

CVE-2026-48504 is unbounded parsing of an inbound W3C baggage header in opentelemetry_sdk BaggagePropagator::extract_with_context. The documentdb gateway (pg_documentdb_gw) ships opentelemetry_sdk 0.30.0 on the 0.114-0 and 0.116-0 lines; 0.117-0 already carries the fixed 0.32.1, and 0.30 to 0.32 is a breaking bump. grep for Baggage over pg_documentdb_gw at v0.114-0 and v0.116-0 returned 0 matches. v0.116-0 installs only TraceContextPropagator (documentdb_gateway_core/src/telemetry/telemetry_manager.rs:100) and parses traceparent itself from the request comment (telemetry/context_propagation.rs:38, no propagator); v0.114-0 installs no propagator at all. The MongoDB wire protocol carries no baggage header, so BaggagePropagator is never constructed. The recipe fails the build if any gateway source names a Baggage type. Verified 2026-10-13.

The advisory is the missing http.MaxBytesReader in the admission webhook handler, knative.dev/pkg/webhook/admission.go:109-117. Easegress reaches knative.dev/pkg only indirectly (go.mod line 382, via knative.dev/serving and knative.dev/client for the FaaS controller) and links API, logging, controller and injection packages of it. Verified with `go list -deps ./cmd/server ./cmd/client` at v2.9.4, v2.10.1 and v2.11.0: 30 knative.dev/pkg packages each, zero under knative.dev/pkg/webhook. The recipe runs the same go list after the build and fails if knative.dev/pkg/webhook is ever linked.

CVE-2026-25727 is stack exhaustion in the time crate when PARSING untrusted input with the RFC 2822 format (parsing::parsable Rfc2822 and its comment combinators), fixed in 0.3.47. time 0.3.46 reaches the image only inside core.wasm of github.com/1password/onepassword-sdk-go v0.4.1 (internal/wasm/core.wasm, go:embed, closed source, used by both 2.11.0 and 2.12.0 go.mod line 195), which external-secrets embeds in /usr/bin/external-secrets. core.wasm keeps a full wasm name section (971494 bytes); grep -aoE '_ZN4time[^ ]*' core.wasm lists 13 parsing symbols and the only well-known parser present is Rfc3339 (time::parsing::parsable ... Rfc3339 parse_offset_date_time); grep -aci rfc2822 core.wasm returned 0, and no time-0.3.46/src/parsing/combinator/rfc/rfc2822.rs source path is present. The RFC 2822 parser is not compiled in. The recipe fails the build if the name section disappears or any rfc2822 symbol appears. Verified 2026-10-13.

CVE-2026-33997 is a privilege-validation bypass in the Moby daemon's plugin installation. The module ships only inside the container plugin's Go worker (libcontainer.so). CVE-2026-113730 (GHSA-crwc-vw2r-qr6m) lets an OGNL EXPRESSION reach blocked methods through java.lang.reflect proxies, bypassing the stricter-invocation block list. It needs the attacker to author the expression text. Here ognl 3.4.4 exists only relocated to org/apache/ibatis/ognl inside mybatis-3.5.19.jar, nested in /etc/guacamole/extensions/guacamole-auth-jdbc-postgresql-1.6.0.jar (checked with unzip -l on the published 1.6.0 image: META-INF/maven/ognl/ognl/pom.properties version=3.4.4; no other ognl copy in any of the image's 83 jars). MyBatis evaluates OGNL only for expressions written in mapper XML: the 21 *Mapper.xml files shipped in that jar hold the only expressions, all constant, e.g. UserPermissionMapper.xml:76 test="caseSensitivity.caseSensitiveUsernames()"; the ${caseSensitivity}/${entityID}/${groups}/${column} placeholders are <include> properties fixed at parse time (SystemPermissionMapper.xml:42-43). Request data reaches MyBatis only as #{...} bound parameter values, never as expression text, and no Guacamole class references org.apache.ibatis.ognl directly (grep of guacamole-auth-jdbc-base-1.6.0.jar). The fix is unreleased for this path: mybatis 3.5.19 is the newest release on Maven Central and still shades ognl 3.4.4 (master moved to 3.4.16, not yet released). Drop this statement when a mybatis release ships ognl 3.4.13 or later inside a Guacamole JDBC extension.

PROVEN false-positive for the flagged component, measured 2026-09-30 on the Joomla 6.1.4 Full_Package. CVE-2024-39912 (GHSA-875x-g8p7-5w27) is a username-enumeration flaw in web-auth/webauthn-lib's ProfileBasedRequestOptionsBuilder: it returns assertion options without allowedCredentials when no user is found. Joomla pins webauthn-lib 4.5.2 exactly on every branch (6.1.4 and 5.4.9 composer.json). Verified on the archive: libraries/vendor/web-auth/webauthn-lib holds 78 PHP files and `grep -r ProfileBasedRequestOptionsBuilder` over the whole Joomla tree returns 0 matches, so the vulnerable class is not present. Joomla builds its own assertion options instead (plugins/system/webauthn/src/Authentication.php getPubkeyRequestOptions, called from PluginTraits/AjaxHandlerChallenge.php). That code has its own, separate behaviour: an unknown username becomes an empty User and gets an empty credential list, exactly like a real user with no passkey, so the response reveals whether an account has a registered passkey rather than whether it exists. Upgrading webauthn-lib would not change that Joomla code path, and it is not the flaw this advisory describes.

PROVEN false-positive, of the 'scanner read the version metadata, not the artifact' kind. The advisory is an Istio AuthorizationPolicy bypass: host matching was case sensitive, so a request with a differently-cased Host header evaded hosts/notHosts rules. It was fixed in 1.9.8 / 1.10.4 / 1.11.1 (2021-08). The authz code this binary links is from istio master four years later, and it carries the remedy: read the source at the pinned commit -- pilot/pkg/security/authz/matcher/string.go at f18fd540c0e8 -- and every string matcher constructor (StringMatcherExact, StringMatcherPrefix, StringMatcherSuffix) takes an explicit ignoreCase parameter and sets StringMatcher.IgnoreCase, which is precisely the case-insensitivity the fix introduced; the pre-fix code had no such parameter. Verified which packages ship, too: `strings` over usr/bin/kgateway shows only pilot/pkg/security/authz/{model,builder,matcher}, the library kgateway's waypoint translation calls to build Envoy RBAC matchers, with no istiod around it. A pseudo-version is therefore the only obtainable form of this module, and v0.0.0-<date>-<sha> sorts below every number the advisory calls fixed, by construction rather than by staleness. The code linked here postdates every one of them by about four years.

PROVEN not reachable with attacker-sized n. GHSA-36hh is unchecked index + n in pyo3 Iterator::nth/nth_back for PyList/PyTuple iterators (pyo3-0.28.3 src/types/tuple.rs:393 `self.index + n`, list.rs:674/869); it needs n near usize::MAX to wrap. pyo3 0.28.3 is linked here only by burner-redis 0.1.7 (docket's in-memory Redis), the newest release, whose code does not build on pyo3 0.29 (downcast renamed; measured with cargo build on 2026-10-13). Checked the burner-redis 0.1.7 sdist: the only list/tuple iterator calls that reach nth are args.iter().skip(1) or .skip(2) on the PyTuple of dispatch_pipeline_command (src/lib.rs:2944, skips at :3021, :3062, :3084, :3109, :3285, :3370, :3538, :3553, :3648, :3659); Skip calls nth with that literal on a fresh iterator (index 0), so index + n is at most 2 and cannot wrap. grep for nth, nth_back, step_by and rev() over src/lib.rs returned 0; the .skip() calls in scripting.rs and store.rs iterate Rust VecDeque/BTreeMap, not pyo3 types. pyo3 0.28.3 itself calls nth/nth_back only in its #[cfg(test)] modules (grep over src/). The recipe fails the build if any .skip() takes another argument or nth/nth_back/step_by/rev appears. Verified 2026-10-13.

PROVEN not exploitable here. GHSA-chgr is PyCFunction::new_closure accepting a closure that is Send but not Sync, so concurrent calls from two Python threads could race on non-Sync captured state. pyo3 0.28.3 is linked here only by burner-redis 0.1.7 (newest release; its code does not build on pyo3 0.29, measured 2026-10-13), and its sdist has exactly one new_closure call (src/lib.rs:402-410): the atexit save hook, which captures an Arc<Store> and a String and only calls store.save(&path). Both captures are Sync: the same Arc<Store> is downgraded and moved into a tokio task at src/lib.rs:416-418, which the compiler accepts only when Store is Send + Sync, and String is Sync. A closure whose captured state is all Sync cannot data-race when called concurrently, which is exactly what the missing bound would have enforced. grep -c new_closure over src/ returned 1. The recipe fails the build if the count changes. Verified 2026-10-13.

CVE-2026-54786 is a host resource leak in the native WASIp1 fd_renumber: a guest loops fd_renumber to exhaust host descriptors, which the advisory says needs a runtime that lets the guest acquire file descriptors (for example by opening a file); runtimes that deny file access are unaffected. wasmtime-wasi 24.0.9 is in /opt/scylladb/libexec/scylla only for WASM user-defined functions (an experimental feature, off unless enabled). At release commit d80b3d6ca26b5457c1b59b47046fab27fa1953f3, rust/wasmtime_bindings/src/lib.rs:194 builds the only WASI context as WasiCtxBuilder::new().build_p1() with no preopened_dir, no inherit_stdio and no inherit_env, and lib.rs:110 links preview1 onto it; grep -n 'preopen|inherit' over that file returned 0 matches. A guest therefore holds only the three virtual stdio descriptors and cannot open a file or socket, so it cannot obtain new descriptors to renumber in a loop. The recipe pins the lock per scylla build and fails on any new build until this is re-checked. Verified 2026-10-13.

CVE-2026-33997 is a privilege-validation bypass in the Moby daemon's plugin installation. trufflehog (main package .) links only the API types and the client from the module, through pkg/sources/docker and go-containerregistry's pkg/v1/daemon: github.com/docker/docker/api, api/types/* and client. Checked with `go list -deps .` at 3.99.2 with docker v28.5.2 (go.mod identical at 3.98.1, same docker pin at 3.97.9): no daemon, plugin manager or API server package is in the build, and trufflehog never calls the client's plugin endpoints. The build fails if a daemon, plugin or api/server package is ever linked. The fix (29.3.1) exists only under the github.com/moby/moby module path, so the +incompatible module cannot be floated to it.

CVE-2026-33997 is a privilege-validation bypass in the Moby daemon's plugin installation. The vCluster syncer (./cmd/vcluster) links exactly one package from the module: github.com/docker/docker/pkg/homedir, a helper that returns the user's home directory, reached through github.com/docker/cli/cli/config/credentials. Checked with `go list -deps ./cmd/vcluster` at v0.37.2 (docker v28.5.2) and v0.35.4 (docker v28.3.3): no daemon, plugin or API server package is in the build.
